::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Jan 31 [1894]  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne  
**Manuscript:** MS Bodleian Library, Oxford: MS English Letters: e.174 ff 165
:::

Dear [Mr Bullock](people/person_221.qmd),
I think [Gordon](people/person_2090.qmd) must have been confirmed, as he was chiefly brought up in England. I see you have marked Bishop Andrews.[^1] Can you tell me of any short biography of him, I have to recommend books for our [Higher Religious Education Society](organizations/other_48.qmd) - books for that era of James I

I doubt [Miss C Coleridge](people/person_329.qmd) having time to write for you. But [Miss Anderson Morshead](people/person_28.qmd) - Industrial School Andover - knew [Bishop Gray](people/person_578.qmd) well, and could write of him Could write of Abp Sancroft[^2] or [Bp Mackenzie](people/person_929.qmd) - whose sister [Anne](people/person_930.qmd) was one of truest saints I ever knew -

I think you should have [Frances Havergal](people/person_2091.qmd) - She was most devout and good, though not High Church, but most attached to the church. Also [Agnes](people/person_2011.qmd) - the devoted workhouse nurse, and I do think [Mrs Trimmer](people/person_2092.qmd) and [Hannah More](people/person_1836.qmd) ought not to be omitted. Also Lady Falkland[^3]

I have a few doubts whether [Miss Sellon](people/person_1294.qmd) realised this saintly ideal. However she fought a great battle

Yours truly
C M Yonge

Would [Miss M Trench](people/person_1418.qmd), the writer of Charles Lowder’s [life](other_books/otherbook_614.qmd) write him for you?

---

[^1]: Endorsed in another hand 'Miss Yonge has been asked to do Abp Sancroft Bp Mackensie R Fanshaw'.
[^2]: This letter, and others to Bullock, relate to his project for a book called *Daily Lections* which was only published in part.   Lancelot Andrewes (1555-1626), bishop of Winchester was one of the proposed subjects of a section, which survives in MS in the Bodleian library and is there catalogued as 'Biographies of Eminent Anglicans'.
[^3]: William Sancroft (1617–1693), archbishop of Canterbury .
[^4]: Later letters make it clear that CMY refers to Lettice Cary, Viscountess Falkland (*c*.1612-1647), rather than her mother-in-law, Elizabeth Cary, Viscountess Falkland (1585-1639), Catholic convert and controversialist.
